official_sources: Habitats regulations assessments protecting a European site
Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017

official_measurement_examples.name: Stage separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: HRA screening asks whether likely significant effects can be excluded; where they cannot be excluded on objective evidence, an appropriate assessment is required. These are distinct stages.

official_measurement_examples.name: Competent authority role
official_measurement_examples.fact: The competent authority makes the Habitats Regulations decision; an applicant's HRA report is supporting evidence and is not the authority's final legal conclusion.

official_measurement_examples.name: Integrity test
official_measurement_examples.fact: At appropriate-assessment stage the competent authority must be able to rule out adverse effects on site integrity before ordinary approval can proceed, subject to the separate derogation route.

official_measurement_examples.name: Derogation separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Alternative solutions, imperative reasons of overriding public interest and compensatory measures form a later derogation route and are not substitutes for screening or appropriate assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: SAC SPA Ramsar context
official_measurement_examples.fact: SAC and SPA data are statutory habitats-site evidence under the Habitats Regulations; Ramsar sites receive parallel national planning protection but their legal provenance must remain distinct.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 PINS currentity
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Inspectorate NSIP HRA advice was updated 14 July 2026; current process guidance does not change the underlying 2017 Habitats Regulations by itself.

official_measurement_examples.name: Plan-level versus project-level evidence
official_measurement_examples.fact: Strategic or plan-level HRA can inform later decisions but does not automatically eliminate the need to assess project-specific effects where they remain relevant.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: HRA status does not determine ownership, exact buildable area, infrastructure capacity or final Future Growth yield for a parcel.

core_rules: screening and appropriate assessment are distinct
applicant HRA is not competent-authority decision
likely significant effect test is precautionary
appropriate assessment integrity test is separate from derogation
derogation requires alternatives IROPI and compensation where applicable
SAC SPA and Ramsar provenance remains distinct
planning permission does not replace HRA
strategic HRA does not automatically clear project effects
guidance update is not legislation amendment
HRA does not calculate development yield
no parcel HRA clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
